dossier.purpose: Open-source (Apache-2.0) AI gateway written in Go: an HTTP server (bifrost-http, React dashboard embedded in the binary), a Go SDK (github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core) and a CLI launcher for coding agents. It fronts 33 provider entries (core/schemas/bifrost.go:94-128) through one OpenAI-compatible API, plus SDK-compat routes for OpenAI, Anthropic, GenAI, Bedrock, LiteLLM, LangChain, PydanticAI, Cohere and Cursor (transports/bifrost-http/handlers/integrations.go:33-51). Features in this tree: weighted API-key pools, retries and fallbacks, governance (virtual keys, budgets, rate limits), request/usage/cost logging in SQLite or Postgres, Prometheus and OTEL, an MCP gateway with Code Mode, optional semantic cache. This checkout is the OSS repo at tag ent-v2.2.4-base; version files read transports 2.2.4, core 1.11.0, framework 1.7.5 (transports/version:1, core/version:1, framework/version:1). The enterprise-only features named at README.md:62-63 live in a separate repository that is not in this tree (docs/changelogs/ent-v2.2.4.mdx:42-44,468-472).

claims.claim: Bifrost is a high-performance AI gateway that unifies access to 23+ providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, and more) through a single OpenAI-compatible API. Deploy in seconds with zero configuration and get automatic failover, load balancing, semantic caching, and enterprise-grade features.
Quick start: 'npx -y @maximhq/bifrost' or 'docker run -p 8080:8080 maximhq/bifrost', then configure via the web UI at http://localhost:8080.
First call is POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions with a provider-prefixed model string, e.g. openai/gpt-4o-mini, and no auth header.
Enterprise deployments unlock adaptive load balancing, clustering, guardrails, MCP gateway and other advanced capabilities (private networking, custom security controls).
Automatic Fallbacks between providers and models; Load Balancing: intelligent request distribution across multiple API keys and providers.
Model Context Protocol (MCP): enable AI models to use external tools (filesystem, web search, databases).
Semantic Caching: intelligent response caching based on semantic similarity to reduce costs and latency.
Governance: usage tracking, rate limiting, and fine-grained access control; Budget Management with virtual keys, teams and customer budgets.
Observability: native Prometheus metrics, distributed tracing, and comprehensive logging.
Secrets management: secure API key management with environment variables and deployment secrets.
Drop-in Replacement: replace OpenAI/Anthropic/GenAI APIs with one line of code, e.g. OpenAI SDK base_url = http://localhost:8080/openai.
In sustained 5,000 RPS benchmarks the gateway added only 11 µs of overhead per request (t3.xlarge; 59 µs on t3.medium); ~10 ns to pick weighted API keys; 100% success at 5k RPS.
Absence: the README does not mention Codex CLI, the Codex SDK, GPT-6, ChatGPT/Codex OAuth accounts, reasoning-effort handling or request compression (all found only in docs/, code and tests).

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - gateway binary built for linux/amd64 (.github/workflows/scripts/build-executables.sh:30-36; release-pipeline.yml:2826), Docker amd64 image (release-pipeline.yml:3054-3063), npx wrapper maps linux x64 to amd64 (npx/bifrost/bin.js:170-173).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no upstream statement about WSL2; only incidental mentions (docs/cli-agents/claude-code.mdx:88, docs/deployment-guides/how-to/install-make.mdx:77). Linux amd64/arm64 binaries and Docker images are published, so a Linux build exists, but WSL2 is not documented or tested.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - darwin/arm64 gateway binary and CLI binary are built (build-executables.sh:31; build-cli-executables.sh:26) and the npx wrapper selects darwin/arm64 (npx/bifrost/bin.js:165-169). Caveat: binaries are cross-compiled on Ubuntu with clang and a downloaded macOS 12.3 SDK (install-cross-compilers.sh:27-69) and no workflow uses a macOS runner (.github/workflows/*.yml runs-on values are ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, codspeed-macro).
platforms.gpu: no - no GPU/CUDA requirement or use found; the gateway is a Go HTTP proxy to remote provider APIs (README.md:15). The only 'gpu' string in product code is in core/providers/replicate/types.go.

integrations.cli: Gateway binary flags -port -host -app-dir -log-level -log-style (transports/bifrost-http/main.go:105-110). Separate 'bifrost' CLI (cli/main.go:19-59; subcommands update, version; flags -config -no-resume -worktree) launches claude, codex, gemini, opencode via a harness registry (cli/internal/harness/harness.go:48-138); documented at docs/quickstart/cli/getting-started.mdx:19-31, not in README.md.
integrations.mcp: Yes. The gateway exposes an MCP server endpoint at /mcp (transports/bifrost-http/handlers/mcpserver.go; docs/cli-agents/overview.mdx:94-132) and acts as an MCP client/agent host with per-client tool filtering and Code Mode (core/mcp/; docs/mcp/code-mode.mdx:176-180); README.md:90.
integrations.sdk_or_api: HTTP API: OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/embeddings etc. (transports/bifrost-http/handlers/inference.go:728-796), WebSocket GET /v1/responses (handlers/wsresponses.go:74-84), SDK-compat routers under /openai, /anthropic, /genai, /bedrock, /litellm, /langchain, /pydanticai, /cohere plus raw /openai_passthrough, /anthropic_passthrough, /azure_passthrough, /genai_passthrough, /chatgpt_passthrough (handlers/integrations.go:33-51), management API under /api/*, Prometheus /metrics (server/server.go:2542). Go SDK: github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core (README.md:169). No Python/TypeScript SDK of its own; Python/JS SDKs are used via base_url (README.md:176-192).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Codex: docs/cli-agents/codex-cli.mdx:29-47 (config.toml model_providers.bifrost with base_url http://localhost:8080/openai/v1, wire_api responses, supports_websockets false, OPENAI_API_KEY set to a Bifrost virtual key; run /logout first, :25-27), :55-70 (HTTPS mode needed for non-OpenAI models), :72-125 (model_catalog_json workaround); docs/runbooks/codex-bedrock.mdx; Bifrost CLI 'codex' harness (cli/internal/harness/harness.go:78-99, native_config.go:99-184); session-id/thread-id headers adopted for key stickiness (core/schemas/useragents.go:84-92; docs/providers/session-affinity.mdx:9); Codex marketplace skill serving (handlers/skills_serving.go:142-147); undocumented POST-only /chatgpt_passthrough/backend-api/codex/responses to https://chatgpt.com (integrations/passthrough.go:52-66); CI runs real 'codex exec' against the gateway (tests/e2e/clis/README.md:5-14,155). Codex SDK: none found. Claude Code: docs/cli-agents/claude-code.mdx, 'claude mcp add --transport http bifrost http://localhost:8080/mcp' (docs/cli-agents/overview.mdx:101), /anthropic route forwards sk-ant-oat OAuth tokens (integrations/router.go:3435-3464).

readme.telemetry_and_network: No product-analytics or phone-home SDK found in core, framework, transports, plugins, cli or ui (searched posthog, segment, sentry, mixpanel, amplitude, DISABLE_TELEMETRY: only MCP-catalog entries, test fixtures and Weaviate compose env). Network the code does perform: (1) provider calls to configured upstreams; OpenAI default https://api.openai.com (core/providers/openai/openai.go:66); optional https://chatgpt.com via /chatgpt_passthrough (integrations/passthrough.go:52-66). (2) Model catalog: GET https://getbifrost.ai/datasheet and /datasheet/model-parameters (pricing, capabilities, parameter allow-lists) at startup and every 24 h (framework/modelcatalog/datasheet/store.go:19-23; config.schema.json:4282-4288); on first boot with an empty DB the fetch blocks startup and failure is fatal (framework/modelcatalog/main.go:149-215; transports/bifrost-http/lib/config.go:5426-5429); file:// URLs support air-gapped use (config.schema.json:4273-4294; examples/configs/withlocalpricingfiles/README.md:1-17). (3) MCP server catalog sync from https://getbifrost.ai/mcp-library, non-fatal, interval 0 disables (framework/modelcatalog/config.go:114; main.go:222-261). (4) Background list-models refresh per provider, default hourly (config.schema.json:4308-4311). (5) The dashboard in the browser calls https://getbifrost.ai/latest-release (ui/lib/store/apis/configApi.ts:73; ui/index.html:8-9). (6) npx wrapper downloads binaries from https://downloads.getmaxim.ai and queries https://getbifrost.ai/latest-release (npx/bifrost/bin.js:9,264); the CLI checks https://downloads.getmaxim.ai/bifrost-cli/latest/version.txt every 24 h unless BIFROST_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 (cli/internal/update/check.go:15-18,50-73; cli/internal/app/app.go:71). (7) Optional sinks only when configured: OTEL, Maxim, semantic cache, Prometheus push, Datadog etc. (transports/bifrost-http/server/plugins.go:274-311). No Bifrost account is required; provider credentials are. Local state: SQLite config.db and logs.db in the app dir (docs/quickstart/gateway/setting-up.mdx:81-85); request/response content is logged by default (lib/config.go:686-687); provider keys are stored in plain text unless an encryption key is set (config.schema.json:43-46). Bind: localhost for the binary (server/server.go:56), 0.0.0.0 in the Docker image (transports/Dockerfile:70-80).

languages: Go (go 1.27.0; core, framework, transports, plugins, cli; CGO + static SQLite for the gateway binary)
TypeScript/React (ui/, Vite, Tailwind 4, Redux Toolkit; built and embedded into the Go binary)

BifrostHTTPServer: bootstrap, route and plugin registration (server/plugins.go:225-326), fasthttp server wrapped by SecurityHeaders, CORS and RequestDecompression middleware (server.go:3087), /metrics at :2542.
Go SDK engine: per-provider request queues, key-pool selection, retry/fallback loop (executeRequestWithRetries ~line 6297), plugin pipeline, MCP manager; module github.com/maximhq/bifrost/core.

Registers SDK-compat routers (OpenAI, Anthropic, GenAI, LiteLLM, Cohere, LangChain, PydanticAI, Bedrock, Typesafe, Cursor) and raw passthrough routers including /chatgpt_passthrough (lines 33-51); WebSocket Responses/Realtime routes.
Native /v1 endpoints: chat, text, responses (+retrieve/delete/cancel/input_items/input_tokens/compact), embeddings, images, audio, batches, files, MCP execution (lines 728-796).
'bifrost' CLI (Bubble Tea TUI): harness registry for claude/codex/gemini/opencode, PTY tab manager, OS-keyring virtual key storage, self-update (cli/internal/app, harness, runtime, secrets, update).

code.architecture: Multi-module Go workspace (go.work is gitignored and generated by 'make setup-workspace': .gitignore:39, Makefile:1832). core/: library engine (bifrost.go: queues, key pool, retries, fallbacks, plugin hooks); providers/<name>/ adapters (openai/ holds Responses and Chat converters plus name-based capability defaults, utils.go); schemas/ shared types (Key, ProviderConfig, context keys, ModelCaps); keyselectors/ (weighted random); sessionaffinity.go; encryptedreasoning.go; mcp/ (client manager, agent loop, Starlark Code Mode). framework/: configstore (SQLite/Postgres), logstore (SQLite/Postgres/ClickHouse request logs with token, cost and latency columns, tables.go:192-282), modelcatalog + datasheet (pricing/capabilities synced from getbifrost.ai), vectorstore, streaming accumulator, tracing, objectstore, plugins (.so loader). transports/bifrost-http/: server/ (bootstrap, plugin registration order prompts, logging, governance, routing, otel, semanticcache, compat, maxim, modelcatalogresolver: server/plugins.go:225-326), handlers/ (inference, governance, providers, logging, MCP server and OAuth, WebSocket), integrations/ (SDK-compat converters and passthrough routers), lib/ (config load, header-to-context conversion). plugins/: 12 separately versioned modules (governance, logging, telemetry, otel, semanticcache, routing, compat, modelcatalogresolver, prompts, maxim, mocker, jsonparser). Request path: fasthttp -> decompression -> integration converter -> middleware -> HTTP plugin hooks -> PreLLM plugins (governance/routing/model-catalog resolver) -> provider queue -> key selection -> provider call -> PostLLM hooks (logging, cost) (AGENTS.md:193-213). Also cli/, ui/, npx/, helm-charts/, terraform/, docs/ and .claude/skills (14 contributor skills).
code.packaging_and_release: Releases are driven by .github/workflows/release-pipeline.yml (push to main or v2.0.0 branch, or manual dispatch; lines 4-7): version files (transports/version etc.) select what to release; the pipeline runs the test jobs, then core/framework/plugin Go module tags, bifrost-http binaries for darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64, windows/amd64 uploaded to a Cloudflare R2 bucket served as downloads.getmaxim.ai (build-executables.sh:30-36; release-pipeline.yml:2766-2906), Docker images maximhq/bifrost (amd64 and arm64 built separately, merged by create-docker-manifest.sh, mirrored to ghcr.io/maximhq/bifrost) plus a UBI9 variant (release-pipeline.yml:2956-3535; transports/Dockerfile, Dockerfile.redhat), changelog push and notification. Other workflows: npx-publish.yml (npm publish --provenance for npx/bifrost and npx/bifrost-cli, lines 54,121), release-cli.yml (CLI tag cli/v<version>, 5 platforms, CGO off, per-binary .sha256 via build-cli-executables.sh:47-54, R2 upload), helm-release.yml, release-bifrost-migration-cli.yml. No checksum, signature or SBOM step exists for the gateway binaries; Docker images rely on buildx default provenance (create-docker-manifest.sh:16-23); no cosign/attestation workflow found. Builds use -trimpath, stripped symbols, static SQLite (build-executables.sh:92-95; transports/Dockerfile:43-48); Docker base alpine:3.23.5 pinned by digest, runs as USER 1000:0, HEALTHCHECK on /health (transports/Dockerfile:54,106,116-117).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: Go testing + testify (gotestsum via Makefile), Newman/Postman provider harness (tests/e2e/api/collections/provider-harness.json, >170k lines), Playwright UI e2e (tests/e2e), vitest (ui), pytest SDK-integration suites (tests/integrations/python, typescript), CodSpeed walltime benchmarks. Approximate file counts: 891 Go _test.go files (core 465, framework 158, transports 105, plugins 104, tests 49, cli 7), 48 UI vitest files, 19 Playwright specs, 10 Python test_*.py files. Notable dirs: core/internal/llmtests (live-provider scenarios), core/internal/mcptests (mock-based agent/MCP tests), tests/e2e/clis (drives real claude/codex/opencode in non-interactive mode against the gateway; CI runs the three most recent CLI releases each run: tests/e2e/clis/README.md:283-301), tests/governance, tests/semanticcache. Workflows (17 files in .github/workflows): release-pipeline.yml (push to main/v2.0.0: core live-provider tests, unit, memory, CLI harness, vLLM, framework, plugins, bifrost-http, migrations, API integrations, cost accuracy, load, Docker image tests, then release); pr-tests.yml and run-core-tests.yml are manual-dispatch only (pr-tests.yml:3-5); automatic on pull_request are only workflow-lint.yml, codspeed.yml and dependency-review.yml; snyk.yml (push, ends with '|| true' at line 78), scorecards.yml (weekly + main), docs-validation.yml, openapi-bundle.yml, e2e-tests.yml (push to one stale feature branch, line 5), dependabot-alerts.yml, pr-test-notifier.yml. All jobs run on Linux runners.

code.security_policy: SECURITY.md exists: report privately via GitHub Security Advisories or email akshay@getmaxim.ai (lines 12-16); acknowledgement within 48 h, updates about every 5 business days, public disclosure typically 30 days after a fix (lines 28-36, 68-79); scope covers core, transports, framework, CLI, official plugins, the maximhq/bifrost image and the UI (lines 81-94); the supported-versions table is stale (transports 1.4.x, core 1.4.x, framework 1.2.x at lines 42-47 vs 2.2.4/1.11.0/1.7.5 in the version files). Separate docs/security.mdx describes Snyk, CodeQL, SHA-pinned Actions, StepSecurity harden-runner and npm provenance.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:15 'Deploy in seconds with zero configuration' (also README.md:21).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs on first boot. With a fresh DB (or no config store) catalog Init fetches the pricing and model-parameter datasheets from https://getbifrost.ai/datasheet[/model-parameters] and returns an error if that fails (framework/modelcatalog/main.go:149-215,262-269; framework/modelcatalog/datasheet/store.go:19-20; datasheet/sync.go:30-49); the caller then logger.Fatal()s (transports/bifrost-http/lib/config.go:5426-5429). file:// pricing_url/model_parameters_url avoid the fetch (transports/config.schema.json:4273-4294; examples/configs/withlocalpricingfiles/README.md:1-17). On later boots with data in the DB the sync runs in the background and failures only warn (framework/modelcatalog/main.go:160-172). Provider keys must still be added, and a key with an empty models list serves no model (core/bifrost.go:9340-9343,9458).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:200-207 'the gateway added only 11 µs of overhead per request' at 5,000 RPS (59 µs on t3.medium).
claim_checks.evidence: Project-reported, not reproduced here. Docs say the runs used mocked OpenAI calls (docs/benchmarking/getting-started.mdx:49-51) and the 'total overhead' footnotes exclude JSON marshaling and HTTP calls (docs/benchmarking/t3.xl.mdx:50-52; t3.medium.mdx:48-50). Marshaling (26.80 µs / 63.47 µs) and response parsing (2.11 ms / 11.30 ms) are separate rows (getting-started.mdx:43-44). README.md:200 gives 11 µs without those qualifiers. The gateway records per-request upstream and overhead latency in its logs (framework/logstore/tables.go:272-275), so the figure can be re-measured.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:85-86 Load Balancing: intelligent request distribution across multiple API keys.
claim_checks.evidence: Selection is weighted random only (core/keyselectors/weightedrandom.go:9-35). Per-key models/blacklist/enabled filters shape the pool (core/bifrost.go:9424-9476). Moving to another key after 429/401/402/403 happens inside the retry loop (core/bifrost.go:6288-6296,6379-6382) whose budget is MaxRetries, default 0 (core/schemas/provider.go:13,634-636), so with defaults there is no in-request key rotation (provider/model fallbacks are separate). Sessions can pin a key and a pinned key is reused on every retry (docs/providers/session-affinity.mdx:47-51,195; core/bifrost.go:9507-9520). Adaptive load balancing and circuit breaker are Enterprise (README.md:63; docs/providers/session-affinity.mdx:88-98).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:106,176-192 Drop-in Replacement: point OpenAI SDK base_url at http://localhost:8080/openai.
claim_checks.evidence: Routes exist for POST /openai/v1/responses, /openai/responses and /v1/responses (transports/bifrost-http/integrations/openai.go:703-707; handlers/inference.go:728,776) and WebSocket GET /openai/v1/responses (handlers/wsresponses.go:74-84), registered by default (handlers/integrations.go:33-51). Codex needs a base URL ending in /v1 (docs/cli-agents/overview.mdx:73; docs/cli-agents/codex-cli.mdx:43) while the Bifrost CLI sets {base}/openai without /v1 (cli/internal/harness/harness.go:86), served by the bare /openai/responses alias. Unprefixed model strings are parsed with an empty default provider (core/providers/openai/responses.go:18) and resolved through the model catalog; if it lists no provider the request fails (plugins/modelcatalogresolver/main.go:62-84,148-165). Docs advise the explicit provider/model prefix (docs/providers/provider-routing.mdx:884-886), and Codex's own model metadata lookup does not know prefixed slugs (docs/cli-agents/codex-cli.mdx:114-125).

claim_checks.claim: docs/quickstart/cli/getting-started.mdx:31,106,195: Codex harness 'Sets OPENAI_BASE_URL'; virtual keys go to the OS keyring, 'never plaintext on disk'.
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the docs. The CLI exports OPENAI_BASE_URL (cli/internal/runtime/runtime.go:26-33) but the repo's own e2e notes say codex 0.146.1 does not read it (tests/e2e/clis/matrix_test.go:488-495; tests/e2e/clis/README.md:101). codexPreLaunch persistently writes openai_base_url, env_key and model into ~/.codex/config.toml and, when a virtual key is set, auth_mode=apikey plus the key into ~/.codex/auth.json (mode 0600) on every launch (cli/internal/harness/native_config.go:99-184; invoked at cli/internal/runtime/runtime.go:71-86). The keyring is used for the CLI's own storage (cli/internal/secrets/secrets.go:11-40) but the key also lands in plaintext in the harness file.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:100 Observability: native Prometheus metrics, distributed tracing, comprehensive logging (and README.md:94 usage tracking).
claim_checks.evidence: GET /metrics (transports/bifrost-http/server/server.go:2542; plugins/telemetry/main.go:1-30). The logging plugin is registered by default when a logs store exists (server/plugins.go:233-246; EnableLogging=true and DisableContentLogging=false in transports/bifrost-http/lib/config.go:686-687). Each row stores provider, model (plus original alias and served model), selected key id/name, virtual key, session id, user-agent/app, token usage, input/output cost, latency and overhead latency (framework/logstore/tables.go:192-282); passthrough responses get usage extracted from /responses bodies (core/providers/openai/passthrough_usage.go:18-30). Cost is skipped when the datasheet has no row for the model (framework/modelcatalog/datasheet/cost.go:2165-2170). OTEL, Maxim and semantic cache load only when configured (server/plugins.go:274-311). Query endpoints /api/logs and /api/logs/stats (handlers/logging.go:376-384).

claim_checks.claim: docs/changelogs/v2.1.0.mdx:70 and v2.2.3.mdx:26: GPT-6 Astra max reasoning effort is preserved; reasoning.effort none is forwarded for gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna while other GPT-6 models keep reasoning on.
claim_checks.evidence: An effort inside the model's ladder passes through unchanged; anything else is snapped to the nearest published level, ties upward (core/schemas/modelcapsreasoning.go:150-196). The ladder is the datasheet row's reasoning_effort_levels, else a name-based default giving every gpt-6 model low/medium/high/xhigh/max (core/providers/openai/utils.go:111-126,132-147,196-203), applied on Responses and Chat (core/providers/openai/responses.go:684-710; chat.go:90-98,238-266). none is forwarded only for gpt-6-sol/-luna; gpt-6-astra and unknown gpt-6 variants are treated as always-reasoning so none becomes low (utils.go:55-70; core/providers/openai/responses_test.go:580-596; harness case 115.1, tests/e2e/api/collections/provider-harness.json:170265-170269). max on gpt-6-astra reaches the wire (core/reasoningeffort_e2e_test.go:26-110; core/providers/openai/responsesmarshal_test.go:179). So effort is preserved when valid for the model, and rewritten otherwise. Outbound bodies can be inspected via extra_fields.raw_request when raw send-back is enabled (transports/config.schema.json:115-119; docs/features/prompt-caching.mdx:411-413).

claim_checks.claim: docs/features/prompt-caching.mdx:31 'Off by default'; need-driven check that request compression is not applied unless chosen.
claim_checks.evidence: Prompt-cache marker injection requires a provider prompt_cache config with auto_inject or injection points (core/providers/utils/promptcache.go:19-34; core/schemas/provider.go:575-597) and a request header cannot opt in by itself (promptcache.go:36-65). No gateway-initiated request, prompt or context compression was found: the only gzip writer is for log object storage (framework/objectstore/gzip.go:15,32; default false at transports/config.schema.json:2222-2224); POST /v1/responses/compact is forwarded as a normal request type (handlers/inference.go:737,796,1804-1819); context_management is forwarded only if the client sends it and stripped for Bedrock (core/providers/openai/responses.go:854-857); inbound gzip/deflate/br/zstd request bodies are decompressed, capped by max_request_body_size_mb (default 100), and never re-compressed upstream (server/server.go:3087; handlers/middlewares.go:233-285,367-396; lib/config.go:693). risks: Not byte-preserving on the OpenAI route. /openai/v1/responses and /chat/completions decode into typed structs and re-serialize (core/providers/openai/responses.go:13-37; types.go:928), then reshape per model capability: reasoning.effort is normalized to the model ladder (responses.go:684-710; chat.go:90-98,238-266), none becomes low on gpt-6-astra and unknown gpt-6 variants (utils.go:55-70), temperature/top_p/logprobs are stripped for GPT-6 (responses.go:772-790,862-896; harness case 115.1, provider-harness.json:170265-170269), service_tier is dropped when the catalog says unsupported (chat.go:185-205), unmodeled top-level body fields are forwarded only via extra_params plus x-bf-passthrough-extra-params (integrations/router.go:779-795), per-key aliases can rewrite the wire model (core/bifrost.go:9459-9461; docs/runbooks/codex-bedrock.mdx:21), and compat flags default to true when a config.json 'client' block omits 'compat' (framework/configstore/clientconfig.go:129-146; fresh installs default false, lib/config.go:682-700) which can drop reasoning/tools/temperature by catalog allow-list (plugins/compat/dropparams.go:140-218). History: GPT-6 Astra max effort was silently downgraded until v2.1.0 (docs/changelogs/v2.1.0.mdx:70,236). Raw /openai_passthrough and /chatgpt_passthrough forward the body as received (integrations/router.go:3497-3519; core/providers/openai/openai.go:8240).

WebSocket Responses forces store=true. handleResponseCreate sets store=true on every response.create unless the OpenAI provider has disable_store=true, replacing a client-sent store:false (transports/bifrost-http/handlers/wsresponses.go:177-191; core/schemas/provider.go:618) although the in-code comment says an explicit client value is respected (wsresponses.go:177-179). The HTTP Responses path only forces false when disable_store is set (core/providers/openai/openai.go:1826-1831). Codex defaults to websocket mode (docs/cli-agents/codex-cli.mdx:57) while the docs and CI configure supports_websockets=false (codex-cli.mdx:46; tests/e2e/clis/matrix_test.go:529-531), so the WS path with Codex is outside the documented and CI-tested setup.

Account pooling covers API keys only. ChatGPT/Codex OAuth logins are not stored or rotated anywhere; the only support is pass-through of the caller's JWT with key selection skipped (integrations/router.go:3435-3464) and Codex docs require /logout so API-key auth is used (docs/cli-agents/codex-cli.mdx:25-27). Key choice is weighted-random (core/keyselectors/weightedrandom.go:9-35); rotation on 429/401/402/403 needs max_retries>=1 but the default is 0 (core/schemas/provider.go:13; core/bifrost.go:6288-6296,6379-6382); allow_direct_keys (default false) bypasses the pool (transports/config.schema.json:266-270). OpenAI encrypted reasoning is bound to the issuing key's organization, so a key change between turns draws a 400 that Bifrost heals by stripping replayed reasoning and retrying once (core/encryptedreasoning.go:191-209; core/bifrost.go:6358-6368; docs/changelogs/v2.2.4.mdx:30). Stickiness comes from session headers only (core/schemas/useragents.go:84-92) and no previous_response_id-to-key binding was found outside WS upstream pinning (transports/bifrost-http/websocket/session.go:15).

Behaviour for new models depends on a remote datasheet. Capabilities, parameter allow-lists, reasoning ladders, pricing and the model-to-provider map come from https://getbifrost.ai/datasheet (core/schemas/modelcapabilities.go:5-23; framework/modelcatalog/datasheet/store.go:19-24), refreshed every 24 h, with name-based fallbacks that treat unknown gpt-6 variants conservatively (core/providers/openai/utils.go:14-70). A bare model absent from the catalog and from hourly live model lists (config.schema.json:4308-4311) fails with an unresolved-provider error (plugins/modelcatalogresolver/main.go:62-84); a model without a pricing row is logged without cost (datasheet/cost.go:2165-2170); first boot with an empty DB is fatal if getbifrost.ai is unreachable (lib/config.go:5426-5429) unless file:// datasheets are configured. When the catalog lists several providers for a bare model the resolver also adds the others as automatic fallbacks (modelcatalogresolver/main.go:96-122).

Defaults favour convenience over hardening. No auth on inference or management APIs until an admin account or enforce_auth_on_inference is configured (transports/bifrost-http/lib/config.go:689; handlers/middlewares.go:1173-1186); the Docker image binds 0.0.0.0 (transports/Dockerfile:70-80; docker-entrypoint.sh:110) while the binary binds localhost (server/server.go:56); prompts and responses are written to logs.db unless disable_content_logging (lib/config.go:686-687; logstore/tables.go:241-244); provider keys are stored in plain text unless an encryption key is set (config.schema.json:43-46); Go .so plugins can be downloaded from a URL into the gateway process (framework/plugins/utils.go:61; soloader.go:36), with unauthenticated callers blocked only by a special-case flag (middlewares.go:1182-1186). The Bifrost CLI persistently rewrites ~/.codex/auth.json (auth_mode=apikey, virtual key in plaintext) and config.toml on every Codex launch, displacing a ChatGPT login mode (cli/internal/harness/native_config.go:131-161).

Release integrity gaps. Gateway binaries are built with no checksum, signature or SBOM step and uploaded to R2 served as downloads.getmaxim.ai (.github/workflows/scripts/build-executables.sh:1-125; release-pipeline.yml:2826-2840); 'npx -y @maximhq/bifrost' downloads and executes that binary without verification and resolves 'latest' from getbifrost.ai (npx/bifrost/bin.js:190-242,264-271,319-363). Only the CLI gets .sha256 files (build-cli-executables.sh:52-54), fetched from the same host and skipped with a warning when missing in the npx installer (npx/bifrost-cli/bin.js:154-167). Docker images get only buildx default provenance (create-docker-manifest.sh:16-23; release-pipeline.yml:3054-3063); no cosign or attestation workflow found. macOS binaries are cross-compiled on Ubuntu with clang and a macOS 12.3 SDK tarball downloaded from a third-party GitHub repo without a checksum (install-cross-compilers.sh:27-45); no macOS or Windows runner exists in any workflow.

Scope and maintenance drift. The tag is an enterprise base tag in the OSS repo; enterprise features are not in the tree. Release cadence is fast: v2.0.0 on 2026-08-26 with breaking changes (docs/changelogs/v2.0.0.mdx:3,24-26) through v2.2.4 on 2026-09-29 (docs/changelogs/v2.1.0.mdx:3, v2.2.0.mdx:3, v2.2.1.mdx:3, v2.2.2.mdx:3, v2.2.3.mdx:3, v2.2.4.mdx:3). Docs and policy lag the code: SECURITY.md lists supported versions transports 1.4.x, core 1.4.x, framework 1.2.x (SECURITY.md:42-47) against 2.2.4/1.11.0/1.7.5 in the version files; AGENTS.md cites core/inference.go and core/mcp.go (absent), 9 plugin modules (12 present) and a checked-in go.work (gitignored, .gitignore:39); docs/security.mdx claims a FIPS base image (transports/Dockerfile:54 is plain alpine), CodeQL scans (no CodeQL analysis workflow; only SARIF uploads at snyk.yml:82,155 and scorecards.yml:92) and Snyk coverage of tests/ (snyk.yml:78 excludes examples,tests and ends with '|| true'). Unit-test workflow pr-tests.yml is manual-only (pr-tests.yml:3-5).

GPT-6 plus Codex coverage is narrower than the claim surface. CI's Codex CLI matrix exercises gpt-5.4, gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.6-sol/-terra/-luna over HTTP with API-key auth, requires_openai_auth=false and supports_websockets=false (tests/e2e/clis/matrix_test.go:307-311,347-351,515-537; tests/e2e/clis/README.md:155). GPT-6 is covered by Go unit tests, one mocked-upstream test (core/reasoningeffort_e2e_test.go:26-110) and live harness folder 115 (provider-harness.json:170265-170267); live-provider jobs need paid keys and run only in the push-to-main release pipeline (release-pipeline.yml:4-7,277-280), not on pull requests. The ChatGPT-OAuth lane has only a route-registration unit test (transports/bifrost-http/integrations/router_test.go:45-60) and no Codex SDK-specific code or docs were found.
